title: Base change and open restriction for separated locally quasi-finite algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S,T,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T,B$ over $S$, let $b:B\to T$ be an $S$-morphism, let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be an $S$-morphism. Suppose that $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale map $h_V\to X$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Suppose also that $f$ is separated: the diagonal $X\to X\times_TX$ becomes a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. The fibre product $X_B=X\times_TB$ is an algebraic space [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every open subspace $O\subseteq X_B$ (its inclusion becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion]), the composite $O\to B$ is again chartwise locally quasi-finite and has diagonal a closed immersion after every scheme base change. In particular these properties hold for $X_B\to B$. If $O$ is represented by a scheme, then $O\to B$ is a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes.

source.place: Tags 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), 03XL (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), 03XK (lemma-composition-quasi-finite); apply composition to the open inclusion. Chartwise local quasi-finiteness is definition-locally-quasi-finite.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $h_U\to X$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the hypothesis on every chart, the scheme morphism $U\to T$ is locally quasi-finite. The fibre product $X_B$ exists as an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $U_B=U\times_T B$. On scheme tests, $h_{U_B}=h_U\times_X X_B$: on a test scheme $H$, a section is a pair $(u,\beta)$ with $f\circ u=b\circ\beta$. For every scheme $D\to X_B$ its atlas pullback is $D\times_{X_B}h_{U_B}\cong D\times_Xh_U$, which is a scheme surjective etale over $D$ by the original atlas definition. Thus $h_{U_B}\to X_B$ is representable surjective etale. The scheme map $U_B\to B$ is locally quasi-finite by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change], applied to $U\to T$ and the arbitrary map $B\to T$.

source.place: Tags 03XL (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite) and 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus), proof: pull back a scheme atlas; scheme permanence is Tag 01TM

proof.text: Let $h_V\to X_B$ be any representable etale chart. The fibre product $W=h_V\times_{X_B}h_{U_B}$ is represented by a scheme. Its projection $p:W\to V$ is surjective etale because it is the scheme test of the atlas from step 1; its other projection $q:W\to U_B$ is etale because it is the scheme test of the chart $V\to X_B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the forward assertion of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality] to $q$ and the locally quasi-finite scheme map $U_B\to B$. Hence $W\to B$ is locally quasi-finite. Since $W\to B$ is also $W\xrightarrow{p}V\to B$, apply the converse assertion to the surjective etale $p$. This proves $V\to B$ locally quasi-finite for every chart, precisely the required chartwise property for $X_B\to B$.

source.place: Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus), proof, reduction to scheme charts and etale source locality; Tag 03XL

proof.text: Write $j:O\to X_B$ for the open inclusion. For a scheme $H\to X_B$, the scheme $O_H=H\times_{X_B}O\to H$ is an open immersion by hypothesis, and hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). For any representable etale chart $h_V\to O$, its composite to $X_B$ is representable etale: on the same scheme test $H$, the pullback is $V\times_O O_H$, a scheme etale over the scheme $O_H$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the composite to $H$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2). Step 2 applies to this chart of $X_B$, giving $V\to B$ locally quasi-finite. Since $V$ was arbitrary, $O\to B$ is chartwise locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 03XK (lemma-composition-quasi-finite), specialized to the open inclusion and expanded by scheme tests; scheme etale inputs are Tags 02GP and 02GN

proof.text: The inclusion $j$ is a monomorphism of sheaves. Indeed, suppose $a_1,a_2\in O(H)$ have the same image $c\in X_B(H)$ for a scheme $H$. They give two sections of the scheme open immersion $H\times_{c,X_B}O\to H$, both lying over $1_H$. These sections are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], so $a_1=a_2$. This proves injectivity on every $H$, which is precisely monomorphy for these set-valued sheaves. The identity inclusion $X_B\to X_B$ is also a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), open-inclusion specialization: its diagonal is an isomorphism, here expressed as injectivity on sections

proof.text:
Take $Y=X_B$ or $Y=O$, and the monomorphism $j_Y:Y\to X_B$ from step 4. Let $D$ be any scheme with a map to $Y\times_B Y$, represented by $y_1,y_2\in Y(D)$ with the same image $\beta\in B(D)$. Let $x_i\in X(D)$ be their images. The scheme test of $\Delta_{Y/B}$ represents equality $y_1=y_2$. On every further scheme test $H\to D$, equality $x_1=x_2$ is equivalent to equality of $(x_1,\beta),(x_2,\beta)$ in $X_B(H)$, and then to $y_1=y_2$ by monomorphy of $j_Y$. Consequently, naturally over $D$,
$$D\times_{Y\times_B Y}Y\ \cong\ D\times_{X\times_T X}X.$$
Here the map $D\to X\times_T X$ is $(x_1,x_2)$; it exists because both $f(x_i)$ equal the image of $\beta$ in $T$. These identifications use the equality description of sheaf fibre products [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The right side is a scheme closed-immersed in $D$ by the assumed separatedness of $f$. Thus the left side is a scheme closed-immersed in $D$ as well [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves the required separatedness of both $X_B\to B$ and $O\to B$ on every scheme test.

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal pullback formula; Tag 03KQ for the monomorphic open restriction, with the equality of the two pullback functors written explicitly

proof.text: Finally suppose $O=h_Z$ for a scheme $Z$. The identity chart of $h_Z$ is representable etale: every scheme pullback is an identity, etale directly from the definition [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Applying step 3 to that chart gives the scheme map $Z\to B$ locally quasi-finite. The fibre product $Z\times_B Z$ is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product]; taking it as the scheme test by the identity map in step 5 says that the scheme diagonal $Z\to Z\times_B Z$ is a closed immersion. This is exactly separatedness of a scheme morphism in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Taking $Y=X_B$ in steps 2 and 5 already supplies the in-particular clause.

source.place: Tag 03KY (lemma-match-separated), definitions on a representable source, and Tag 03XJ (definition-locally-quasi-finite)

proof_origin.place: Tags 03KL and 03KQ for diagonals; Tags 03XL, 0ABM and 03XK for local quasi-finiteness via charts, with scheme source locality from descent.tex Tag 03X4.

lean.statement: theorem space_separated_lqf_permanence {S : Scheme.{u}} (T B : Over S) (b : B ⟶ T) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X.obj ⟶ (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.obj T) (hqf : ∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ f.hom)).left) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal f.hom)) : IsAlgebraicSpace (Limits.pullback f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)) ∧ (∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ (Limits.pullback f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).obj), IsEtale a → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom)).left) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom) ∧ ∀ (O : AlgebraicSpace S) (j : O.obj ⟶ Limits.pullback f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) j.hom → (∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ O.obj.obj), IsEtale a → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ j.hom ≫ (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom)).left) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal (j.hom ≫ (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom)) ∧ ∀ (Z : Over S) (e : yoneda.obj Z ≅ O.obj.obj), IsSeparated (yoneda.preimage (e.hom ≫ j.hom ≫ (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom)).left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (yoneda.preimage (e.hom ≫ j.hom ≫ (pullback.snd f ((Scheme.fppfTopology.over S).yoneda.map b)).hom)).left
